# Decision Grade

> A public framework for making AI-assisted professional work more decision-ready before reliance.

Decision Grade is earned through a defined full review for one declared use. It is not a permanent property of a document or a guarantee of correctness. Work beyond the reviewed material—including synthesis, scenarios, backcasting, implications, and recommendations—should be described as more decision-ready. The aim is a stronger basis for judgment with the source, evidence, assumptions, reasoning, limits, and epistemic distance made visible.

External research on this site supports the problem. It does not prove that any particular system outperforms a strong direct model review or a qualified human reviewer.

## Framework pages

- [A stronger basis for a decision](https://decision-grade.ai/introduction): The core reframe. A polished, cited document can still fail the decision it was written to support. Decision Grade is narrow and use-bound; decision readiness is the broader goal.
- [The problem](https://decision-grade.ai/the-frame): Why citations, coherence, and a correct endpoint do not establish that the route to a conclusion is sound. Introduces epistemic distance and the boundary between reviewed material and later authored work.
- [Current evidence](https://decision-grade.ai/evidence): Active 2026 research on professional adoption, partial support, stepwise reasoning, long workflows, and multi-agent handoffs, with the task and limit attached to each result.
- [What Decision Grade means](https://decision-grade.ai/the-doctrine): The use-bound determination, what it says, what it does not say, and why later analytical work cannot inherit the label.
- [Questions to ask before relying](https://decision-grade.ai/buyers-checklist): Ten evidence-oriented questions for reviewing an AI-assisted document, internal build, direct model review, or verification vendor. No universal score or invented threshold.
- [Reliance lanes](https://decision-grade.ai/lane-discipline): Volume and Decision as intended reliance contexts. Rapid may triage in either lane but cannot clear Decision work; Full is required before consideration and does not automatically clear it.
- [What to measure](https://decision-grade.ai/watchlist): Comparative quality, recall, precision, stability, decision usefulness, repair value, failure handling, and the discipline required for scenarios and watches.
- [About](https://decision-grade.ai/about): Independence, evidence policy, authorship, and publisher-interest disclosure.
- [MCP server](https://decision-grade.ai/mcp): Public, read-only access to the framework through `https://decision-grade.ai/api/mcp`.

## Publisher disclosure
